currentContext.expansion: Anant Raj Limited is scaling its data centre and cloud services business through a phased capacity build-out. As of March 2026, the Company has operationalised 28 MW IT load across two campuses: Manesar (21 MW) and Panchkula (7 MW). A third campus at Rai, Sonipat, with a planned capacity of approximately 200 MW IT Load, has commenced work and will be operationalised in phases. The Company has also signed an MoU with the Government of Andhra Pradesh for a new 50 MW IT load data centre facility, expanding its footprint into South India. With this addition, total planned data centre capacity reaches 357 MW IT load, of which 117 MW IT load is targeted to commence by FY 2028. The overall roadmap aims to scale capacity to 357 MW by FY 2032. In real estate, the Company is advancing its township development pipeline at Anant Raj Estate, Sector 63A, Gurugram, with multiple phases and group housing projects under construction or in approval stages.

risks.risk: Concentration of executive power and family control
risks.note: The Sarin family (Amit, Aman, Ashim) hold all executive director roles and chair key committees (CSR, Share Transfer, Finance & Investment, Risk Management), creating potential governance and succession risks.

risks.risk: Business restructuring and demerger execution risk
risks.note: A Demerger Committee was constituted post-year-end to evaluate restructuring options for the Real Estate and Data Center businesses, introducing uncertainty around operational continuity, capital allocation, and stakeholder impact.

risks.risk: Real estate sector cyclicality and regulatory risk
risks.note: As a real estate developer, the Company is exposed to demand cycles, interest rate sensitivity, and evolving regulatory frameworks (e.g., RERA) that can materially impact project viability and cash flows.

risks.risk: Data center business concentration and technology risk
risks.note: The strategic pivot into data centers exposes the Company to rapid technological obsolescence, high capital intensity, and dependence on a few large clients or hyperscalers.
The Risk Management Committee explicitly includes cyber security risks in its oversight framework, reflecting the heightened threat landscape for real estate and data center operations.

one-line thesis: Anant Raj has transformed from a real estate player into a diversified infrastructure giant with Data Centers and sovereign cloud now contributing 28% of H1 FY26 revenue, driven by $1.1B QIP funding and 63MW capacity by Dec '26 — this shift materially de-risks the business and unlocks high-margin recurring revenue streams.
financial scorecard: revenue: +24.22% YoY (H1 FY26: ₹1,223cr); EBITDA/margin: +43.17% YoY, margin up to 27.23% (H1); PAT (rptd): +34.28% YoY (H1: ₹264cr); PAT (normalized): same as reported (no one-offs); order book: not disclosed; net debt: net cash positive (₹1,100cr QIP + ₹100cr warrant conversion - ₹125cr debt prepayment)
guidance: revenue growth: Data Center to reach ₹1,200cr by FY27; margin: 75% EBITDA margin for DC; order inflow: 63MW by Dec '26, 117MW by FY28; capex/commissioning: ₹700cr total DC capex, 35MW new capacity under development, Rai 20MW by Dec '26, 100MW Greenfield by FY28
segment / subsidiary detail: Data Center: H1 FY26 revenue ₹58.42cr (Colo ₹44.55cr, Cloud ₹13.87cr); EBITDA ₹75cr (75% margin); 8MW Colo fully handed over, 0.5MW Cloud operational; Real Estate: ₹1,164.78cr revenue (H1); 3 launches planned (Estate IV, Group Housing 1 & 2); 5.1cr sq.ft. total pipeline under RERA/LOI
growth verticals / optionality: 117MW DC capacity by FY28; Cloud expansion from 14MW to 36MW; SaaS/PaaS layer monetization (revenue doubling potential); 307MW total DC target by FY32; Stellar Resorts redevelopment (7.5M sq.ft.); Delhi commercial entry (7L sq.ft. by FY28)
margins & cost dynamics: Colo EBITDA margin: 75%; Cloud EBITDA margin: 75%; Cost per MW: ₹50cr total, ₹26cr incremental; Cloud revenue: ₹12cr/month/MW; Colo revenue: ₹90L/month/MW; Power pass-through excluded in Colo revenue accounting
capex / expansion: ₹700cr total DC capex (H1 FY26: ₹187cr added); ₹35MW new capacity under development; ₹20MW at Rai under construction; ₹100MW Greenfield planned for FY28; Real Estate capex: ₹322cr pending for Group Housing
capital allocation: Net cash positive; prioritized DC expansion (₹1,100cr QIP + ₹100cr warrant conversion); zero debt policy maintained; no new debt planned; real estate kept low-leveraged; future capex funded internally
risks & watch-items: Cloud demand visibility reliant on govt. data sovereignty laws (pending); MeitY empanelment delayed (expected Nov '25); real estate launch timing risk (Q4 approvals pending); sovereign cloud adoption pace vs. private hyperscalers
management quality / tone: Highly confident, bullish on DC/cloud trajectory, proud of zero-debt status, emphasizes disciplined execution, avoids forward guidance but confirms all targets are on track, tone is assertive and visionary
non-obvious takeaways: Cloud revenue per MW (₹12cr/month) is 13x Colo's (₹90L/month) — yet same 75% margin, implying massive unit economics advantage; real estate revenue is largely from Anant Raj Estate (legacy) while DC is the future; 8MW vacant capacity in 63MW DC is strategic buffer for Cloud conversion

themes.title: Data-Center & AI electrical/cooling buildout
themes.need: AI/data-center capex pulls transformers, switchgear, gensets, HVAC/cooling, optical and cabling AND a new high-margin cooling supply chain. CUMMINSIND flags DC at ~30-35% of domestic powergen with a demand surge since Oct-2025; VENUSPIPES won a ~INR185cr DC-cooling LOI; AEROFLEX building liquid-cooling skids; BLUESTARCO on DC MEP; STLTECH/NETWEB on optical + HPC/AI servers (STLTECH's DC+Enterprise mix hit 21% of Q1FY27 revenue from 1% in FY26 on record INR13,100cr quarterly order intake anchored by a $1.1bn multi-year hyperscaler deal; FY27 EBITDA-margin guide raised 20%->23% and DC+Enterprise mix guide raised 30%->50% of revenue); REDINGTON/DCI/IVALUE on GPU/AI-infra distribution. Q1FY27 added two balance-sheet-scale entrants: HCLTECH is putting up to INR 3,500cr into its own AI-datacenter business with a 50MW long-term ambition ('megawatt isn't the product, it's the anchor'), and RELIANCE disclosed a 168 MW Meta data centre at Jamnagar built on its own balance sheet.
themes.driver: DC cooling LOIs converting (VENUSPIPES, AEROFLEX); hyperscaler/colo India capex (CUMMINSIND gensets, BLUESTARCO MEP); STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler optical-connectivity deal and 2.4x QoQ order-book jump to INR18,618cr; GPU/AI-infra orders.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Favourable policy measures, including lower interest rates, GST rationalisation, and continued government focus on housing and infrastructure development, are expected to strengthen affordability, improve liquidity, and support demand in the real estate sector.
- Rising urbanisation, increasing disposable incomes, preference for quality developments, and expanding connectivity infrastructure are expected to drive growth across key markets.
- India's data centre capacity is expected to expand significantly from around 1.5 GW currently to 5-8 GW by 2030, positioning India as a key global hub for cloud, AI, and digital infrastructure investments.
- The hospitality sector is expected to benefit from strong occupancy levels, with pan-India premium hotel occupancy projected to remain at 72-74% in FY 2025-26.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Anant Raj Limited is scaling its data centre and cloud services business through a phased capacity build-out. As of March 2026, the Company has operationalised 28 MW IT load across two campuses: Manesar (21 MW) and Panchkula (7 MW). A third campus at Rai, Sonipat, with a planned capacity of approximately 200 MW IT Load, has commenced work and will be operationalised in phases. The Company has also signed an MoU with the Government of Andhra Pradesh for a new 50 MW IT load data centre facility, expanding its footprint into South India. With this addition, total planned data centre capacity reaches 357 MW IT load, of which 117 MW IT load is targeted to commence by FY 2028. The overall roadmap aims to scale capacity to 357 MW by FY 2032. In real estate, the Company is advancing its township development pipeline at Anant Raj Estate, Sector 63A, Gurugram, with multiple phases and group housing projects under construction or in approval stages.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demerger] A Composite Scheme of Arrangement has been approved by the Board of Directors to demerge all Data Centre and Cloud operations into Ashok Cloud Pvt. Ltd., creating two independently listed companies — Anant Raj Limited (real estate and infrastructure) and Ashok Cloud (digital infrastructure and cloud services). Stated benefits: greater strategic focus, unlocking shareholder value, and a simplified corporate structure.
- [Demerger — entitlement] "Eligible shareholders will receive 1 equity share of Ashok Cloud (FV ₹2) for every 1 equity share of Anant Raj (FV ₹2) held on the record date."
- [Credit rating] "Infomerics Valuation and Rating Ltd. has upgraded rating of the Company to 'A- Stable' outlook."
- [International] "Established outreach in Singapore by commissioning of Anant Raj Cloud Singapore Pte Ltd for sourcing clients from South East Asia and rest of the world" — described elsewhere as a 100%-owned Singapore subsidiary for international business development.
- [Empanelment / partnerships] Empanelled with MeitY as a Sovereign Cloud service provider and with BSNL as a Data Centre service provider; TIA Tier III certification cited; cloud services delivered "in association with Global Partner" (the partner is not named in the extracted text). A JV with Birla Estate Private Ltd (Birla Navya) covers 191 residential plots planned in 4 phases with 764 luxury independent floors. TARC Ltd was demerged from Anant Raj Ltd in 2020.
